descriptionHi: बारिश भरे रविवार में एक नाई और उसका नियमित ग्राहक आधुनिक जीवन के अस्तित्वगत संकट पर बात करते हैं।

title: Manasanamaha
description: A young man revisits 3 relationships in an inventive meditation on memory and love.
descriptionHi: एक युवक अपने 3 रिश्तों को याद करते हुए स्मृति और प्रेम की अनोखी यात्रा पर निकलता है।

title: Arjun
description: A blind preschooler dreams of gifting his teacher a painting in this Filmfare-winning story.
descriptionHi: एक दृष्टिबाधित बच्चा अपनी शिक्षिका को चित्र भेंट करने का सपना देखता है - साहस और कल्पना की फ़िल्मफ़ेयर-विजेता कहानी।

title: Vishaad
description: A weary inspector's routine inquiry at a reclusive scientist's house turns into an encounter with memory and grief itself, in this lyrical meditation on loss and time.
descriptionHi: एक थका हुआ इंस्पेक्टर एक अकेले वैज्ञानिक के घर की जांच करने पहुंचता है, और उसकी तफ़्तीश धीरे धीरे स्मृति और शोक के साथ एक अनकहे मुक़ाबले में बदल जाती है। समय और खोए हुओं को याद करने की चाहत पर एक भावुक कविता जैसी फ़िल्म।

title: The Monkey’s Paw | W. W. Jacobs की खौफनाक क्लासिक कहानी
titleHi: The Monkey’s Paw | W. W. Jacobs की खौफनाक क्लासिक कहानी
description:
क्या हो अगर आपकी हर इच्छा पूरी हो सकती हो… लेकिन हर इच्छा की अपनी एक कीमत हो?

The Monkey’s Paw, W. W. Jacobs की 1902 में प्रकाशित प्रसिद्ध क्लासिक हॉरर कहानी है—एक ऐसी कहानी जिसने “Be careful what you wish for” वाले विचार को horror literature की सबसे यादगार अवधारणाओं में बदल दिय

title: Writing Doom – Award-Winning Short Film on Superintelligence (2024)
titleHi: Writing Doom – Award-Winning Short Film on Superintelligence (2024)
description:
*UPDATE* Hey all! Just a note to say that my new film Seat at the Table is now out!
https://youtu.be/qHpnWiBHHaU?si=7O9Q4KCjQazpfuVa

I've been blown away by all the love for Writing Doom over the past year and a half, and I really hope you enjoy the follow-up :)

~

Writing Doom is a fiction short film about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI).

Grand Prize Winner - Future of Life Institute's Superintelligence Imagined Contest
https://futureoflife.org/project/superintelligence-imagined

A writing team are given the task of making Artificial Superintelligence the 'bad guy' for the next season of their TV show. With the help of a newcomer to the team (a Machine Learning PhD), they must figure out how and why an ASI might function as an antagonist - and the threat it might pose to humanity.

To find out more about AI:
https://futureoflife.org/resource/introductory-resources-on-ai-risks/

Written & directed by Suzy Shepherd https://suzyshepherd.co.uk

Cast:
Max - Adam Lloyd-James
Jerry - Mike Kelson
Gail - Amantha Edmead
Anders - Aleksander Varadian
Mimi - Imogen Westwood Flood
Producer - Esmee Cook

Crew:
Director of Photography - Richard Allen
Gaffer - Wil Thong
First assistant camera - Jamie Evans
Sound recordist - David Head
Make up - Holly-Rose Tomlinson
Runner - Sebastien Fletcher-Biddle
Editor - Suzy Shepherd

Scientific Advisors:
Samuel F. Brown
Isaac Dunn

Music:
Slow Momentum by Mark Fabian (premiumbeat)

With thanks to Eliezer Yudkowsky, whose words, arguments, and explanations I drew upon heavily while writing the script.

Festival awards:

GRAND PRIX: SHORT FILM at the Director Talents Movie Awards 2024/5
https://newdirectorawards.com/winners1/202425

BEST DIRECTOR (Long Short Category) at the AltFF Alternative Film Festival
https://www.instagram.com/alternativefilmfestival/p/DH1H5lBPTSF/

title: RODENT | Award-Winning Post-Apocalyptic Short Film | Featuring Art Malik
titleHi: RODENT | Award-Winning Post-Apocalyptic Short Film | Featuring Art Malik
description:
In the not-too-distant future, a rat journeys through the last vestiges of humanity as it searches for food for its family. But when it encounters a formidable threat, the true scale of what has happened to our world begins to emerge.

Written and directed by filmmaker Joe Fereday, RODENT is a post-apocalyptic short film blending real animal behaviour with narrative drama to explore a dystopian future through an unexpected point of view.

Featuring the voice acting talents of actor Art Malik, RODENT has been selected for 36 film festivals across three continents and 10 countries, earning nine nominations and four awards, including Audience Choice, Best Cinematography and Best Short. Its festival run includes five BIFA-qualifying, two Academy Award-qualifying, two Canadian Screen Award-qualifying and one BAFTA-qualifying festival - bringing natural history filmmaking into the drama festival circuit.

RODENT was the winning concept in Silverback Films’ internal short-film competition - an initiative created to give people across the company the opportunity to experience the full filmmaking process and bring an original idea from pitch to screen, with funding, mentorship and production support from Silverback.

Subscribe to Silverback Films for exclusive access to the filmmaking, science, and craft behind groundbreaking natural history: 
👉  https://www.youtube.com/@Silverback_Films?sub_confirmation=1

About Silverback Films
We tell the greatest natural history stories on Earth. Our world-class filmmaking team produces landmark series and films, combining extraordinary wildlife cinematography with powerful storytelling to inspire audiences worldwide.

Nature. It’s what we love. It’s what we do.

title: Mother's Sacrifice to Save Her Child | Nube | Oscar-Qualified Animated Short Film
titleHi: Mother's Sacrifice to Save Her Child | Nube | Oscar-Qualified Animated Short Film
description:
What would you do to stop your child from falling?

In a poetic world where clouds live, love and eventually rain, Noma, a soft white cloud, discovers that her daughter Mixtli may be in danger of raining too soon.

NUBE is a heartbreaking 3D animated short film about motherhood, fear, sacrifice and the impossible instinct to protect the person you love most. Directed by Christian Arredondo Narvaez and Diego Alonso Sánchez de la Barquera Estrada, this award-winning fantasy animation turns the life cycle of clouds into a moving story about maternal love, loss and letting go.

🎬SYNOPSIS: After witnessing an old dark stormy cloud painfully rain and die in sorrow, Noma, a puffy white cloud realizes that Mixtli, her daughter, a dark stormy cloud, is in danger of raining prematurely.

🔎ABOUT THE FILMMAKERS: Diego Alonso Sánchez de la Barquera Estrada: Animator and director born in Mexico city, I started my journey in the world of animation as a motion designer where I spent 12 years directing advertisment spots for TV. In 2018 I went to Gobelins to study a Masters of Arts in Character Animation and Animated Filmmaking. Along Christian, oodirected NUBE, my first shortfilm.

Christian Arredondo Narvaez: Animation director and illustrator, I graduated in 2020 from the Master of Arts in Character Animation and Animated Filmmaking at Gobelins, l’Ecole de l’Image. Since 2009 I have dedicated myself entirely to the visual arts. In 2015 I began my career as an animator participating in different projects that include short films, feature films and video clips.

title: Crash Site | A Sci-Fi Short Film Starring Steven Yeun and Sam Richardson
titleHi: Crash Site | A Sci-Fi Short Film Starring Steven Yeun and Sam Richardson
description:
When a mysterious object crashes to Earth, two friends make a chance discovery -- unaware that they’ve just set off a chain of events that will thrust them into a race against time to uncover the object's true purpose before it's too late. 

🎬 Title: Crash Site
🧠 Genre: Sci-Fi / Thriller / Mystery
⏱️ Runtime: 14 minutes

Starring: Steven Yeun, Sam Richardson

Directed and Edited by Jason Sperling
Written by Miles Brandman
Produced by Ursula Camack
Cinematography by Sean Ware
Production Design by Jason Hougaard

#shortfilm  #scifi  #indiefilm  #sciencefiction  #firstcontact  #alienartifact  #crashsite  #stevenyeun #samrichardson #twd #indiefilmmaking #indiefilmmaker #vfx #vfxshorts #film #movie #space #kickstarter #thriller #mysterybox #mystery #noai #film #dust #filmfestival #viral 

🎥 About This Film: Funded via Kickstarter and filmed in just four days with a crew of friends, this short is a scrappy tribute to the sci-fi films we grew up with. 

🏆 Film Festivals & Screenings: Crash Site was selected to screen at the following festivals and curated platforms:
• Official Selection — DUST (Curated Sci-Fi YouTube Channel, 2026)
• Official Selection — Boston Sci-Fi Film Festival (2026)
• Official Selection — Las Cruces International Film Festival (2026)

📡 A Note From the Director: Sick of AI storytelling? I can assure you no AI was used in the making of my new short film Crash Site. Why, you ask? Are you against it morally and philosophically because AI will replace us all!?! No, no nothing like that. I didn’t use AI because in reality, this short film is not really new. It was shot a long time ago (2013) and while I had gotten very far into post on it, there was always one last thing to do. So now after more than 10 years, I finally got it done, without AI. Whew. It stars Steven Yeun and Sam Richardson giving awesome performances and is a true labor of love from a small crew of friends and a throwback to a time before AI existed and we made movies with people about people discovering and using things that have power beyond their control. Hmmm, sounds like something I know…Enjoy and thanks for watching our short film! -- Jason Sperling

🔗 Connect:
Follow Us on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/crashsiteshort/
Follow Us on Twitter:  https://x.com/crashsiteshort
Visit our Website: https://www.crashsitefilm.com/

title: MANEKI | Full Lesbian Short Film
description:
Aiko, a young cashier working at a ramen restaurant, gets rejected by Jean, Aiko’s favorite regular. But when Jean returns to the restaurant and tries to bridge the gap, Aiko must reconcile her feelings as their relationship enters uncharted territory.

Official Selection
Austin Film Festival
Outfest Fusion
Asian American International Film Festival
San Diego Asian Film Festival
Boston Asian American Film Festival
Santa Monica International Film Festival

If you ask someone out, and you get rejected, can you still be friends? That's the question we sought to answer with this cute, light-hearted coming-of-age film.

title: Still Here (還在) | Award-Winning Sundance Documentary Short Film
titleHi: Still Here (還在) | Award-Winning Sundance Documentary Short Film
description:
In Kaohsiung, Taiwan, a few residents refuse to leave their now-abandoned village.

A selection of Short of the Week, the web's leading curators of quality short films.

SUBMIT A FILM: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/submit/
FULL REVIEW: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/2020/04/30/still-here/

Subscribe to S/W on YouTube!
Website: http://www.shortoftheweek.com
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ShortoftheWeek
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/shortoftheweek
Twitter: https://twitter.com/shortoftheweek

Still Here
Directed by Sean Wang
https://www.seanwangfilm.com/

"What makes a house a home? For me, it’s the things inside it that shape our memories and, as is often the case, it’s the ones which are long gone that I cherish and miss the most. Like the ugly shelving unit in my childhood bedroom, which our dog managed to climb once to get to a tub of Nutella, the mermaids I drew on the flowery wallpaper near my pillow, or the kitsch figurines my grandparents had collected on their travels, that I would examine for hours.

Sean Wang (3,000 Miles) also felt compelled to revisit his roots in his tenderly observed and deeply personal documentary short Still Here. Shot in a remote village in Taiwan, the nine-minute film uses compositional brilliance to paint a compelling portrait of the fragility of our physical homes, and exudes compassionate intimacy for both the individuals who appear in it and the spaces around them. The result both breaks and warms the heart.

In a village in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, there are just 6 residents left. Refusing to move away from their beloved, but now almost entirely abandoned village, around them, what were once homes which housed happy and thriving families, are now empty structures, slowly crumbling to dust. Still Here pays homage to the past by turning each scene into a cinematic work of art, hanging in its 4:3 frame. The emptiness it depicts is haunting but the characters ground the mood with their positive attitudes and persuasive charm.

“Still Here was filmed in the village where my grandmother lived, my mother grew up, and where I spent my childhood summers”, Wang explains to S/W as we discuss the motivation behind his short. “Nine years ago, my grandmother moved out of the village. Recently, I discovered that not only did nobody move into my grandmother’s house after she left, but that the entire village had been displaced and decayed for years, except for a few residents who refused to leave. I was curious to find out what their lives were like now that the village was abandoned — and why they decided to stay”.

Still Here brought back so many bittersweet memories, since I too spent many happy summers in my own grandparents’ village as a child. The early ones of my family around the fire, or collecting apples in the heat, of laughter, singing and the neighbour’s dogs barking in the distance, were soon replaced by the sight of empty streets and the sour smell of an unloved house. A feeling that will be familiar for many around the world.

Sean Wang performs a powerful balancing act by weighing the heavy emptiness of the abandoned houses, against the abundance of life in the characters he interviews. With their fascinating stories, impressive collections of knick-knacks and wool sweaters, and their stubborn refusal to be brought down by the sadness spreading around them, the residents of Kaohsiung are impossible not to love. Their spirits lift the otherwise achingly somber documentary, just like they bring life into the otherwise entirely dead village, making us smile while holding back the tears." - S/W Curator Serafima Serafimova

Director / Editor: Sean Wang
Producers: Cynthia Lee, Pamela Li, Sean Wang
Cinematographer: Zach Stoltzfus
Composer: Breton Vivian
Production & Post-Production Sound: Michael O' Connor
Colorist: Kinan Chabani

title: Drawn to You - Animated Short Film
titleHi: Drawn to You - Animated Short Film
description:
Young Emily didn’t see anything wrong with her drawing of two girls holding hands, but her mother saw otherwise and tore both the paper and her child’s heart in two. Little did they know, the drawings had come alive and are determined to reunite with one another across the vast bedroom of pages, no matter what risk comes their way. An adventurous and heartwarming tale, “Drawn to You” shows audiences both the struggles and joy that comes with being true to your heart, and not letting others tell you who to be.

title: WUSS: Big Boys Don’t Cry 🏆 Award Winning Short Film
titleHi: WUSS: Big Boys Don’t Cry 🏆 Award Winning Short Film
director: Short Frame: Award Winning Short Films
description:
WUSS is an award-winning drama short film about childhood loss, vulnerability, and the pressure to “be strong.” When a young boy is abandoned by his father and his beloved cat goes missing, he sets out on a quiet, emotional search that forces him to confront grief, self-blame, and the feelings he’s been taught to hide.

This powerful coming-of-age short film explores masculinity, emotional repression, bereavement and what it means to grow up being told that “big boys don’t cry.” Through an intimate, child-centered lens, WUSS captures the heartbreak of loss and the courage it takes to feel.

An award-winning indie short film from the festival circuit, WUSS is a moving, human story for fans of emotional drama and character-driven storytelling.

If you enjoy heartfelt short films about childhood, family, and resilience, this film is for you.
-

Whether it's Drama, Documentary, Horror, Sci-Fi or Comedy, Cannes, Berlin, Sundance or first time filmmakers: Short Frame is home to the best short films from the world’s most innovative filmmaking talent.

title: Code Red | Award Winning Coming-Of-Age Short Film on Period
titleHi: Code Red | Award Winning Coming-Of-Age Short Film on Period
description:
Code Red is a whimsical, coming-of-age short film that confronts the lack of easy access to period products that girls face in school. When sixth grader, Karman, gets her period for the first time at school she skips class with her best friend, Tiffany, to go on a quest in search of a menstrual pad. Throughout the film, Karman’s experience is intercut with metaphorical imagery that illustrates the feelings girls experience during that “time of the month.” It’s a fun and bold way to show the bittersweetness of growing up and bring awareness to the issue of period poverty.

descriptionHi:
Code Red is a whimsical, coming-of-age short film that confronts the lack of easy access to period products that girls face in school. When sixth grader, Karman, gets her period for the first time at school she skips class with her best friend, Tiffany, to go on a quest in search of a menstrual pad. Throughout the film, Karman’s experience is intercut with metaphorical imagery that illustrates the feelings girls experience during that “time of the month.” It’s a fun and bold way to show the bittersweetness of growing up and bring awareness to the issue of period poverty.

With family, you're either in...or you're out.

title: BURROW: A Soldier Discovers Himself 🏆 LGBT Short Film - AWARD WINNING
titleHi: BURROW: A Soldier Discovers Himself 🏆 LGBT Short Film - AWARD WINNING
director: Short Frame: Award Winning Short Films
description:
LGBT Drama Short Film starring Christian Coulson (Harry Potter) and Marc Crousillat. Believing himself to be one of the last survivors left in the wake of extinction, an ex-war soldier finds unexpected comfort with the arrival of a weary traveler, forcing him to reckon with his long avoided sexuality. 
-
ABOUT SHORTFRAME: We curate a selection of award winning short films; the best short films direct from the film festival circuit. Whether it's Queer Drama, Documentary, Horror, Sci-Fi or Comedy, Cannes, Berlin, Sundance or first time filmmakers: Short Frame is home to the best short films from the world’s most innovative filmmaking talent.
-
BURROW is directed by Leaf Lieber and published with the permission of the filmmakers. The film screened at film festivals including Tribeca Film Festival and Melbourne Queer Film Festival. It was the winner of the Colin Higgins Youth Filmmaker Grant presented by Frameline and was a finalist at the 2021 Shore Scripts Film Fund.
-
DIRECTOR'S BIO: Leaf Lieber is a NY/LA based director originally from Kauai, Hawaii. Lieber’s organic and visceral worlds often exist at the intersection of fantasy and reality, tackling themes of grief, transformation, and queer identity. He is currently developing his debut feature film. 
-
Burrow | Drama, LGBTQI+ | United States
©  Leaf Lieber - Published with permission
-

title: LGBTQ Short Film | Odd Bird
description:
Odd Bird is an award-winning lgbtq short film from Katy Dore.  Crafty Short Films presents new award-winning short films every week with our filmmakers receiving 100% of the ad revenue their film generates on YouTube! Subscribe, like and comment to support Crafty’s mission to discover, highlight and support independent filmmakers.

Odd Bird Logline: As a boy, Clark always felt like the odd bird in his conservative ranch family. To cope, he created a comic book, "The Adventures of Odd Bird," making himself the hero of his own story. Now 19, a publisher is interested in his work and Clark needs to return home to get the comic manuscript...and tell his mom his truth. Clark fears once he tells her he's gay, he won't be welcome there again.

#lgbtq #lgbt #shortfilm #comingoutstory #queer #indiefilm #filmfestival #film #novel 

Tune in every Tuesday and Thursday for new short films every week on Crafty!

ABOUT CRAFTY:
Crafty Short Films presents snack-sized stories, both narrative and non-fiction with, with an emphasis on heart and humanity with a new short film every Tuesday and Thursday! 

Crafty aims to highlight and discover talented filmmakers while also providing filmmakers with 100% of the YouTube Ad revenue that their film generates! Our team loves the film festival scene and the sense of community that comes with it. Our goal is to bring that curated experience to your living room each and every day by connecting audiences with fellow film enthusiasts and filmmakers around the world. 

Crafty (or craft services) is a little snack on a film set. It’s the thing filmmakers need to keep themselves going. But it also describes the mentality of our filmmakers who have to get crafty in order to tell their stories. Crafty is made by filmmakers for filmmakers and film loves alike.

title: Unexpected Item | Award Winning Short Film | Romantic Comedy
titleHi: Unexpected Item | Award Winning Short Film | Romantic Comedy
description:
A supermarket. A self-service checkout. The strangest piece of life advice you'll get all week.

Subscribe to our YouTube channel ▶ https://www.youtube.com/@CenterFrame

Henry can't bring himself to ask out the cashier he likes. At the self-service till, the machine starts talking back... unsolicited, oddly empathetic, surprisingly persuasive. Whether he's losing his mind or finally finding it is a question for you to answer after watching the film.

Director Stephen Gallacher leans into magical realism with a colour-drenched, vibrant world. The tone is warm without being cute. Olivia Colman voices the till (and she's having a great time with it).

Jamie Blackley plays Henry on the front foot of his own awkwardness, with Isabella Laughland as the cashier and Andrew Ellis as Sid.

Unexpected Item won Best Film at Anaheim International and Cambria, Best Comedy Short at Orinos and Independent Short Awards, Best Short Film at Vegas Movie Awards and Falcon International, and Best Romantic Comedy at Top Indie Film Awards, with selections at Norwich, Carmarthen Bay, Queen Palm, Austin Comedy and JellyFest.

A short film about courage, connection, and the small voices that push us toward each other.

---------

Directed by Stephen Gallacher, written by Chris Croucher.

Starring
Jamie Blackley – Henry
Isabella Laughland – Nicky
Andrew Ellis – Sid
Olivia Colman – Till

title: Oscar® nominated short film "Shok" | Drama about friendship and loyalty during war - by J. Donoughue
titleHi: Oscar® nominated short film "Shok" | Drama about friendship and loyalty during war - by J. Donoughue
description:
Short drama on friendship and loyalty during war | "Shok" - by Jamie Donoughue

Based on true events, "Shok" is set during the escalation of the Kosovan War when the country was occupied by Serbia...

Two young Kosovan boys, Petrit and Oki, are the best of friends. After Oki buys a bike, Petrit is desperate to have one of his own. Ever the businessman Petrit finds a niche dealing cigarette papers to the occupying Serbian troops. However with tensions and violence escalating in the country, many would see this as traitorous. Building a steady network of contacts, Petrit drags Oki into ever more dangerous situations until their lives are put at risk. As their relationship is tested to the limits they begin to encounter the true intentions of the Serbians and learn the meaning of friendship.

This short film has won the following awards:

- Aspen Shortsfest – Best Drama (Grand Prize)
- Aspen Shortsfest – Youth Award
- Aspen Shortsfest – Audience Award
- Hollyshorts Film Festival – Best Drama (Grand Prize)
- DC Shorts Film Festival – Outstanding Live Action Drama (Grand Prize)
- DC Shorts Film Festival – Audience Award
- Manhattan Shorts (Worldwide Film Festival) – Silver Award
- CinEast International Film Festival– Audience Award
- San Jose International Short Film Festival – Best Drama (Grand Prize)
- Thess International Film Festival – Cinematic Achievement Award
- SwiKos Film Festival - Best Short Film (Grand Prize)
- SwiKos Film Festival - Cinematography Award
- Interfilm Berlin International Film Festival – Best Film (Confrontations OL Award)
- Mallorca International Film Festival - Best Actors Award
- Festival Tous Courts International Film Festival - Audience Award

title: Loving Silence (2024) | Award-Winning Queer Short Film
titleHi: Loving Silence (2024) | Award-Winning Queer Short Film
description:
An award-winning LGBTQ+ romantic drama about love, regret, and second chances, set entirely at a silent retreat.

Starring JJ Bozeman and Addy Marsh.

Official selection at DC Shorts, Minneapolis St. Paul International Film Festival, KASHISH Mumbai, Cinema Diverse Palm Springs, OutSouth, and more.

When Jerome runs into his old flame, Luke, at – of all places – a silent retreat, their past threatens to unravel his present.

"A fantastic showcase of subtle, silent acting... Loving Silence exemplifies the power of storytelling that makes shorts so special." — Metro Weekly 
(https://www.metroweekly.com/2025/09/dc-shorts-film-festival-2025/)

Website: https://www.lovingsilencefilm.com

Instagram: @lovingsilencefilm

Letterboxd: https://letterboxd.com/film/loving-silence/

IMDB: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt32907221/?ref_=pro_tt_visitcons

If this film resonated with you, leaving a comment genuinely helps independent films like this reach new audiences through YouTube's recommendation system!

_

LOVING SILENCE (2024) was a small but meaningful endeavor – a true labor of love – with a small self-funded budget, created in collaboration with a tiny-but-mighty team who all believe in its story. The project is a proof of concept for a feature written in 2023, which in its making demonstrated its own merits as a stand-alone piece.

The core production team was only five people: myself (writer, director, producer), Jett Cain (the director of photography), Colin Barry-Jester (production sound), Claire Bridget Martin (actor and production coordinator), JJ Bozeman (lead actor) and Addy Marsh (lead actor) and we only had about two days to shoot on location on the grounds of Gather Greene in upstate New York in April of 2024. I genuinely believe what we were able to achieve with a strong but bare bones crew, in such a short window of time is remarkable.

The vision was to tell a truly unique queer love story – one rich with humor and catharsis, staged in an unusual and visually striking setting – with almost no dialogue. The final product, I believe, delivers on that premise and proves this story not only works, but offers something truly fresh.

Since shooting it, it’s been on a whirlwind of a journey, showcasing at film festivals between 2024 - 2026 in New York (Hudson Film Festival, ArtsFest Film Festival [WINNER: Best Director, Best Picture, NOMINATED: Best Cinematography, Best Performance], Peekskill Film Festival), California (Cinema Diverse Palm Springs LGBTQ Film Festival), Minnesota (Minneapolis St. Paul International Film Festival), North Carolina (OutSouth Queer Film Festival, Flourish at Charlotte Pride), Washington D.C. (DC Shorts International Film Festival), and Mumbai, India (KASHISH Mumbai International Queer Film Festival).

Whether you discovered the film through a festival screening or are watching it here for the first time, thank you for giving it your time.

Thank you,
Nick Perlman
Writer/Director

title: Brotherhood | Oscar Nominated Short Film by Meryam Joobeur
titleHi: Brotherhood | Oscar Nominated Short Film by Meryam Joobeur
description:
One of the most acclaimed shorts of recent memory—a 2020 Oscar nominee, and a Shorts Award Winner. Mohamed is a shepherd in rural Tunisia with his wife and two young sons. Their world is shaken when the oldest son returns after a long journey with a mysterious woman he says is his wife. 

A selection of Short of the Week, the web's leading curators of quality short films.

SUBMIT A FILM: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/submit/
FULL REVIEW: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/2019/10/02/ikhwene-brotherhood/

BROTHERHOOD (Ikhwène)
Written and Directed by Meryam Joobeur
Midi La Nuit, Cinetelefilms, Travelling Distribution
https://www.facebook.com/BrotherhoodShortFilm/

Subscribe to S/W on YouTube!
Website: http://www.shortoftheweek.com
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ShortoftheWeek
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/shortoftheweek
Twitter: https://twitter.com/shortoftheweek

"I do not fault the detractors and skeptics who proclaim that "Brotherhood" should be dismissed as merely representing this year’s archetypal festival drama—a pejorative term to some that indicates the kind of serious short film that confuses dourness with profundity, and is best understood as some young director’s try-hard bid to get their government film board to pony up for their feature debut. Let’s review the case: set in a locale exotic to the majority of elite fest-going cinephiles? Check. Tense and explosive family dynamics? Check. Gorgeous, yet restrained, cinematography? Check. Oh, and a sometimes languorous 25min runtime? Double-check! As a defense however to those critics and haters—watch the film. You’re wrong. Watch the film again.

While "Brotherhood" exhibits the trappings of a type of film that we often deride as “festivally”, it is really hard in my mind to contest its exquisiteness. It is highly specific in its character and world-building, buoyed by the authenticity of its writer/director, Meryam Joobeur, whom is of Tunisian descent, and by the capable performances of its first-time actors (their casting, central to conception of the film, is recounted here). As pure drama, the film delivers, inculcating mystery early on, then building to a devastatingly emotional climax. Finally, in theme, it pulls off the nice trick of being both topical and timeless: confronting complex contemporary issues, like religious extremism, with the tried and true spirit of a Greek tragedy. 

Filmmakers have made hay for generations in porting the classics to film, from works as different as Laurence Olivier’s seminal Shakespeare adaptations to Clueless. Brotherhood is not an adaptation, but it is working with the same raw materials as Sophocles and Seneca—the defiance of one’s father, questions of honor, the inability to communicate with loved ones through the haze of anger, and, ultimately, betrayal...

... Continue reading the entire review here: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/2019/10/02/ikhwene-brotherhood/ " 
-S/W Curator Jason Sondhi

title: GASLIGHTING | Award-winning short film
description:
The short film is about a dangerous form of manipulation. Gaslighting means one person overpowers another by manipulating their perception – through unsettling lies, flustering projection and constant guilt-shaming. Such mental and emotional abuse keeps the victim confused and conditioned on the gaslighter. At the end the protagonist emancipates in a surprising way.

title: The truth is out there. (2021.2022 Festival Official Selected)(3D animation short film)(Maya)
titleHi: The truth is out there. (2021.2022 Festival Official Selected)(3D animation short film)(Maya)
description:
On this sunny day, the ants were industriously going about their business, but suddenly a massive shadow covered the sun, causing the ants to halt in surprise. They were curious about what could have caused this interruption to their day.

Some of the ants brought up a legend they had heard about creatures known as humans, which were said to be larger and more powerful than ants. This idea filled the ants with fear and uncertainty, and they held a heated discussion about the existence of these humans.

The king of the ants was livid upon hearing about the talk of humans. He forbade any further discussion about them and proclaimed that the ant king was the greatest in the world. Despite his efforts to squash the truth, the truth is still out there.
--

2022 ASIFA-East 52nd Animation Festival Official Selected

titleHi: CHOPSTICKS | One minute award-winning short film | Canon R8
description:
A college student struggles to master his chopsticks.

GEAR:
Canon R8
EF 50mm f/1.8 lens at 2.8 with Viltrox EF to RF adapter
I can't remember what ISO, but somewhere between 2000-3500.
Shot in Clog 3

THOUGHTS ON THE R8:
This is a very powerful camera for independent amateur filmmaking. The camera has terrific low-light performance and terrific autofocus. The lack of in-body stabilization was not an issue, because I used a tripod. Overall, this camera is terrific and will do wonders for your film projects. I can't wait for my next project.

title: NANNY | SHORT FILM | Higgsfield Global Film Festival #higgsfieldai
titleHi: NANNY | SHORT FILM | Higgsfield Global Film Festival #higgsfieldai
description:
"NANNY" FILM BY LILIT MOVSISYAN FOR  Higgsfield Global Film Festival

Synopsis
Between her mother's two jobs, a girl grows up in a cinema seat, the only place her mother trusts to leave her while she takes a nap.
The place that quietly ends up raising her. Years pass, and somewhere along the way, she stops just watching.

NANNY: a story about love that shows up in unexpected places, made entirely inside Higgsfield. 

#higgsfieldai #HiggsfieldGlobalFilmFestival #higgsfield 



Director's Statement

I'm Lilit Movsisyan, an award-winning filmmaker from Armenia. For most of my career, I envied painters, they could simply take a canvas into their own studio and create, without waiting on financing, without the enormous logistics a film usually demands.

With Higgsfield, that gap has closed for me. I finally have a studio of my own, one where a story like NANNY doesn't have to wait for a budget to exist. 

NANNY isn't just about a mother and daughter going to cinema, it's about every mother who gave everything she had, in circumstances she didn't choose, so her child could have something more. This film is my way of saying thank you, to her, and to every mother like her.

description:
LGBTQI+ Drama Short Film. During a snowy Chinese Spring Festival, a chance encounter between a postman Aiden and Jerome, a man with a traditional Chinese background, leads to a heartfelt conversation that results in a newfound understanding between the two.
-
ABOUT SHORTFRAME: We curate a selection of award winning short films; the best short films direct from the film festival circuit. Whether it's Queer Drama, Documentary, Horror, Sci-Fi or Comedy, Cannes, Berlin, Sundance or first time filmmakers: Short Frame is home to the best short films from the world’s most innovative filmmaking talent.

UNTITLED US is directed by Thomas Mai and published with the permission of the filmmakers. It screened at festivals including Festival du Nouveau Cinéma, Vancouver Asian Film Festival and Lift off Toronto Film Festival.
-

A graduate of Emily Carr University of Art + Design, he has worked across narrative films, commercials, period pieces, and music videos. His work is driven by a passion for visual storytelling and a desire to explore filmmaking across cultures, with the goal of working internationally as a cinematographer.

title: Auntie Issues | Award-Winning LGBTQ Short Film
titleHi: Auntie Issues | Award-Winning LGBTQ Short Film
description:
🔔 Subscribe for more award-winning films! @ShortFilmBox 

Lola and Veronica are psychology students, and their conversations tend to get a little therapeutic. One day, after a philosophy class like any other, Veronica, who is in love with their teacher and vents about it to Lola, has a revelation: she likes older women because she was in love with her aunt when she was a child!

Writer & Director: Rita Hostt and Tadeo Pestaña Caro
Country: Argentina
Key Cast: Rita Hostt, Nuria Wassaf, Coni Marino, and Ale Granado
Genre: Romantic Comedy
Runtime: 14 min.
Production year: 2023
Original Language: Spanish

Subtitled: English, French, Japanese, Korean, Turkish, Arabic, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Russian, Portuguese, Romanian, Italian, Polish.

Watch more short films here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCKIpEHArOA0tXlagax31LfGIDIKIXf1_

Director's Statement: "Auntie Issues is a project born from the need to tell different stories. As a community, we are shaped by prejudices against people who feel and think outside the norm — but there are a lot of us “weirdos”! This project aims to contribute to the visibility of the bisexual community, which remains marginalized even within the LGBTQI+ collective, as well as to the practice of self-managed creation. It’s a very personal story, a sort of self-portrait in which, hopefully, many other people will also see themselves reflected." - Rita

description:
Shruti Madhur is an award-winning Bengali short film which tells the story of a couple married for seven years and how they deal with the intrusion of an outsider, a face from the past.

Produced by Saptaswa Basu under Neo Studios, the film is directed by R Chattopadhyay and features Unmesh Ganguly and Apala Chowdhury in the lead roles. With soulful music and playback by Ishaan, lyrics by Baarish, and a strong technical team behind the camera, Shruti Madhur presents an intimate and emotionally resonant cinematic experience.

title: TAMO JUNTO - Award-Winning Short Film
description:
(eng below) - O projeto não seria possível sem o esforço de todos os gigantes artistas e amigos. São 16 anos trabalhando na industria de animaçao para finalmente ter a possibilidade de viabilizar uma produção dessas aqui do brasil. É um pequeno curta independente mas tem um enorme significado para mim. A arte salva e continua me salvando todos os dias. Agradeço ao carinho e abraço dessa galera de peso. #TAMOJUNTO

Tamo Junto é um curta-metragem independente de animação. Em dias de medo, Dois vizinhos passam a tornar cada momento de interação como grandes preciosidades. O trabalho conta com a voz do rapper Criolo e da atriz Luciana Silveira, e com a participação de Emicida. A trilha sonora é assinada pela Loud+. Durante a produção, o curta foi uma tentativa de cura através da arte.

- The project would not be possible without the efforts of all the giant artists and friends.  It's an independent short film but it is a huge acomplishment for me.  Art saves lives and keep saving me every day. I am grateful for the love of this heavyweight team. #TAMO JUNTO

Tamo Junto is an independent animated short film by flooul animation.  2 neighbors lean on each other, turning small moments of life into great treasures. Voices by Criolo, Luciana Silveira and Emicida. Original Soundtrack By Loud+

descriptionHi:
(eng below) - O projeto não seria possível sem o esforço de todos os gigantes artistas e amigos. São 16 anos trabalhando na industria de animaçao para finalmente ter a possibilidade de viabilizar uma produção dessas aqui do brasil. É um pequeno curta independente mas tem um enorme significado para mim. A arte salva e continua me salvando todos os dias. Agradeço ao carinho e abraço dessa galera de peso. #TAMOJUNTO

Tamo Junto é um curta-metragem independente de animação. Em dias de medo, Dois vizinhos passam a tornar cada momento de interação como grandes preciosidades. O trabalho conta com a voz do rapper Criolo e da atriz Luciana Silveira, e com a participação de Emicida. A trilha sonora é assinada pela Loud+. Durante a produção, o curta foi uma tentativa de cura através da arte.

- The project would not be possible without the efforts of all the giant artists and friends.  It's an independent short film but it is a huge acomplishment for me.  Art saves lives and keep saving me every day. I am grateful for the love of this heavyweight team. #TAMO JUNTO

Tamo Junto is an independent animated short film by flooul animation.  2 neighbors lean on each other, turning small moments of life into great treasures. Voices by Criolo, Luciana Silveira and Emicida. Original Soundtrack By Loud+

Top 10 do Público / Awdience: 30º Kinoforum - Festival Internacional de Curtas Metragens de São Paulo 2019

description:

titleHi: Panjurli | Award Winning Kannada Short Movie | English Subtitles
description:
Panjurli is an award-winning Kannada short movie set in the coastal regions of Karnataka exploring the divine art of DAIVAARADHANE with a thriller touch.

We would like to thank all the supporters and Red FM short film festival team. Panjurli is our new Kannada short film. KiKi team has been putting a lot of efforts and has also won 2 awards for best Acting and Cinematography and was also nominated for Best Music and Editing for the year of 2020 in Red FM short Film awards held at Mysore.  

Kindly use headphones for better sound experience as all the tracks in this short movie has been designed originally for the scenes.

Official Selection for DadaSaheb Phalke International Film Festival - 2023, Goa Short Film Festival and premiered at “Short TV” platform incorporated in London, England.

title: Award-Winning Stop-Motion Animated Short Film | Tokri (The Basket)
titleHi: Award-Winning Stop-Motion Animated Short Film | Tokri (The Basket)
description:
▶️ Submit your Short Film: https://www.shortverse.com/submit

A clumsy accident leads a young girl to the streets of Mumbai in the hope of making things right from Indian animators, Studio Eeksaurus. 

_TOKRI_
Directed by Suresh Eriyat

While a relatively simple story, grounded in the lived experience of India's destitute, Tokri overflows with detail. The scale of the production is truly remarkable—we adore stop-motion, with over 100 films in our collection, but despite the overwhelming diversity of subjects and styles you'll encounter while traversing the catalog there are a few commonalities to the majority of them: tight compositions, confined spaces, relatively few characters. These decisions are often right for the story, but they are also a compromise to the pain-staking nature of the craft, an attempt to reduce complexity within scenes. An unusual degree of motion abounds within even simple scenes in Tokri, and Eriyat and his team are unafraid of going wide as well, in shots that seek to depict the cacophony of the Mumbai streetscape and which encompass dozens of moving elements. We always love a good stop-motion timelapse, and the video below gives you a good sense of the undertaking. 

FULL REVIEW: https://www.shortoftheweek.com/2020/07/08/tokri/

title: SANSEDAI (三世代) - Award Winning Documentary Short Film
titleHi: SANSEDAI (三世代) - Award Winning Documentary Short Film
description:
Through intimate conversations over old photobooks and home movies from the 1930s, sansedai (三世代) explores themes of identity and belonging as it follows the filmmaker’s 92-year-old grandmother’s journey growing up during war, migrating to a country that was once deemed an enemy, and what it means to be Japanese-American.

Director’s Statement:
As a self-taught filmmaker, I was always drawn to the power of visual storytelling and fell in love with the medium of film. Shortly after graduating college, I took a leap of faith and moved to NYC to immerse myself in the film community. Now years later, I’ve worked my way up through the camera department in both NYC & LA and I am proud to share my first documentary short film, sansedai (three generations).

This film shares the very personal story of my grandmother growing up during the war in Japan before moving to the US in the 1950s amidst heightened racial tensions, especially towards Japanese people. My grandmother’s wedding kimono connects all three generations and tethers me to my ancestral heritage as I try to define what being Japanese-American means to me.

This timely documentary illuminates the lasting impacts of war and imperialism while sharing a first hand account of the uncertainties of migrating to a new country. As a proud granddaughter of immigrants, I hope this film resonates across generations and cultures as we continue to see the humanity in others.

If you would like to make a donation to help support this film & the incredible team that helped bring it to life, you can donate here: https://buymeacoffee.com/sansedai

title: LEILA | Award-Winning Emirati Short Film (2024)
description:
LEILA is a coming-of-age short film about identity, courage, and the quiet rebellion of choosing your own path.

Released in 2024, this short film follows a young woman standing at the fragile intersection between tradition and self-discovery, where expectations feel heavier than dreams.

Leila has always known who she is. The problem is that everyone else seems to know who she should be. As familial pressure tightens and cultural expectations loom, she is forced to confront the cost of obedience and the risk of freedom. What begins as quiet doubt turns into an internal reckoning, unfolding through moments of silence, restraint, and emotional vulnerability.

LEILA is not a story about rebellion for the sake of it. It is about the courage it takes to define yourself when the world has already defined you.

Official Selection
First-Time Sessions Volume 2 – Lift-Off Global Network (Festival Release 2023)

Winner
Appreciation Award – Al Ain International Film Festival (2024)

Written, Directed, and Produced by Saif Al Hadhrami

If this film resonated with you, continue the conversation. Share it with someone who has ever felt torn between expectation and self-definition.

title: Hangout | Short Film | Kabeer Khurana - 4k
description:
A creatively uninspired musician (Romi) is compelled to create a musical masterpiece when he has a conversation with a social activist (Alia). Set in a locked down world, Romi and Alia linger on a Zoom call after their company announces pay cuts across the board. The ensuing conversation leads to revelations - both, about one another, and about the world they inhabit. Seeing Alia's steadfast commitment toward less privileged people, Romi is inspired to write a song, the royalties of which are used to help send some migrant workers back to their homes. The film is about a gentle kindling of hearts, and the power of union between two individuals who are world apart.

Written and directed by Kabeer Khurana
Produced by Simran Lakhanpal, Ramneek Sawhney and Humaramovie

title: A Bird in Passage | Short Documentary | Manish Sachdeva
titleHi: A Bird in Passage | Short Documentary | Manish Sachdeva
description: 'A Bird In Passage' is a short documentary film based on life and the art of Shri Puran Bhat, a traditional puppeteer from India. Originally from Rajasthan, his group of puppeteer families settled in Delhi almost fifty years ago. They lived in the Kathputli Colony at Delhi, an artist community. Which has been collapsed due to government policies. Puran Bhat was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2003, given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama but now he doesn’t have a roof and this artist community is struggling to save their existence.

title: Hangovers of Intimacy | Short Film | Divyam Chadha | Kabir Jai Bedi | DCF
titleHi: Hangovers of Intimacy | Short Film | Divyam Chadha | Kabir Jai Bedi | DCF
description:
The narrative ‘Hangovers of Intimacy’ is set around the side effects of indulgence. ‘The Morning After’ raises some difficult questions that are mostly unsaid and rarely answered. Here’s an exploration of precisely that. 
The character at play is a manifestation of all the minds that oscillate between the two contradictory needs for both attachment and detachment.

Writer and Director: Divyam Chadha
